title: FSB Chair sets out FSB work on AI and stablecoins
source_used: Financial Stability Board press release (read in full)
key_facts: The Financial Stability Board (FSB) published a letter from its Chair, Andrew Bailey, to G20 Finance Ministers and Central Bank Governors ahead of their 15 October meeting.
The letter highlights heightened volatility in sovereign bond markets, vulnerabilities in private credit markets and risks related to AI.
It is accompanied by a note on global stablecoin arrangements covering cross-border vulnerabilities and monitoring.
The FSB is also submitting finalised sound practices for responsible adoption of AI, which incorporate feedback from a public consultation.
The release says safe AI adoption across the financial system will remain an important feature of the FSB's agenda next year.
Other reports sent to the G20: a peer review on public sector backstop funding for banks, a consultation on regulatory and supervisory modernisation, and an implementation monitoring review.
The FSB brings together national authorities from 24 jurisdictions; Bailey is Governor of the Bank of England.
The release does not describe the specific AI risks named in the letter.
quote_evidence: The letter highlights risks to the global financial system, including heightened volatility in sovereign bond markets, vulnerabilities in private credit markets and risks related to artificial intelligence (AI).
Finalised sound practices for responsible adoption of artificial intelligence (AI), incorporating feedback from the public consultation.
The rapid pace of development means that focusing on safe adoption of AI across the financial system will remain an important feature of the FSB’s agenda next year.
why_it_matters_hint: The main international coordinator of financial rules puts AI on the G20 finance agenda and finalises its responsible-use practices.
